title: People
purpose: The right number of trained people on every floor, every shift, with a deputy behind each seat. No phone goes unwatched. Nothing waits on one person.
how: One anchor per 10 phones. One supervisor per 50. A trained bench of 10%, the way phones carry a 10% spare pool. Per 1,000 hours a day that is about 300 phones, 30 anchors, 6 supervisors, and 5 reviewers. Past 10 rigs one person cannot sweep every 30 minutes and still check angles and storage; restarts slip, angles drift, and the flag rate climbs. Moharam owns the bench and moves it between sites. Portfolio Managers call it.

Everyone enters through Mano. Referral or application, a screen, an interview with the manager who owns the seat, papers and the gate, day one, then a first shift. No papers, no start, no matter who vouched. Moharam assigns site people to books. Anyone can refer; the hire reward pays once the person is onboarded and working.

Every role has a day-one module with a length, a trainer, and a sign-off line. Anchors, two hours. Supervisors, one day. Portfolio Managers, one week. Runners, one hour. QC reviewers, a calibration set. Nobody works the role before the line is signed, and the signed sheet lives in the onboarding file with Mano.

Absence by 10 PM the night before, by call and message to the Portfolio Manager. No reply in 20 minutes, call Moharam. A no-call, no-show is immediate removal from the project, no steps. The rule is hard because a missing anchor is 10 phones unwatched from the first cycle.

Every seat has a named deputy, written down before the first shift, who has done the module for that role. Founders included. The deputy is who acts when the seat is empty for an hour or a month, so nothing waits on one phone number.

Housing for workers brought in from another city is a bridge. It exists only where a site opens before local hiring lands, and it ends seat by seat as local hires sign off on day one. Mano books it. The site's Portfolio Manager hires the locals.

procedures.name: Hiring through the gate
procedures.owner: Mano, with the manager who owns the seat
steps: Screen every referral and application the same week: age, ID, where they can work, which seat.
The manager who owns the seat interviews. Anchors and supervisors: a Portfolio Manager. Runners and the bench: Moharam. Reviewers: Youssef Medhat. The store and the hubs: Mano.
Papers before anything else: offer letter, contract, ID copy, consent, fraud briefing sign-off, one account in their name. Half a gate is no gate.
Day-one module with the trainer for the role, signed off, filed with the papers.
Moharam assigns site people to a book. The first shift is paired with a senior in the same role.

procedures.name: Sizing a site's team
procedures.owner: Moharam and Mano, at central planning
steps: Phones divided by 10 is the anchor count. Round up.
50 phones or more adds a supervisor, one per 50.
Add 10% of the floor to the book as bench, hired through the gate before Day 0.
Write a deputy against every seat, the Portfolio Manager's included, in the site plan.
No site launches short. A missing anchor on Day 0 means Day 0 moves.

procedures.name: Day one, per role
steps: Run the module before the first shift, or on Day 0 with Mazen at a new site.
Show, then watch: the trainee does every step on a live phone while the trainer watches the first full 30-minute cycle.
Cover escalation last: who to call, the 20-minute rule, and the three universal rules.
Both sign the line. The sheet goes to Mano the same day.

procedures.name: Absence and cover
steps: Take the call and the message before 10 PM. Reply within 20 minutes, or the next call goes to Moharam.
Call the bench that night. Confirm the cover by name and device number before you sleep.
No cover: split the phones across the anchors on site for the shift and tell Moharam before clock-in.
Log the absence and the cover in the wrap report.

procedures.name: No-call, no-show
steps: No call and no message by 10 PM the night before, and nobody at clock-in, is a no-call, no-show. At clock-in the supervisor, or the senior anchor where there is no supervisor, splits the missing anchor's phones across the anchors on site, then makes one call.
Tell Moharam the same morning. Removal is immediate, no steps.
Mano closes the account and the papers the same day. Gear comes back within 24 hours; final pay follows inspection.
The bench fills the seat by the next shift. Mano opens the seat for hiring the same day.

procedures.name: Housing as a bridge
procedures.owner: Mano, with the site's Portfolio Manager
steps: Book housing only when a site opens before local hiring lands, and only for the seats not yet filled locally.
Local hiring for those seats starts on Day 0 through the gate. Referrals from the site's own staff first.
The day a local hire signs off on day one, housing for that seat ends. The brought-in worker moves to the bench or the next launch.
Count housed seats at the weekly book review until the count is zero.

procedures.name: Leaving
steps: The person tells their manager. The manager tells Mano and Moharam the same day and confirms the deputy by name before the last shift.
Gear returns to the Portfolio Manager or Mano within 24 hours. Final pay follows inspection.
Account closed, wearer log and registry updated, the same day.
The deputy holds the seat. Mano opens it for hiring the same day and updates the map.
A person removed for fraud is never re-enrolled, under any name or device.

breaks.do: No word by 10 PM the night before and nobody at clock-in is a no-call, no-show: removal, same day, and Moharam hears the same morning. The supervisor and the anchors on site split the phones for the shift. The bench fills the seat by the next shift.

Operators wait 20 minutes, then call Moharam. Moharam takes the book's calls himself for the day. If the Portfolio Manager is still silent by the wrap report, Moharam puts the pre-named deputy on the book in writing that evening. Supervisors hold the floor; nothing pauses.

breaks.what: A site opens before local hiring lands
breaks.do: Housing bridge. Mano houses the brought-in team near the site. Local hiring starts on Day 0 through the gate, and housing ends seat by seat as locals sign off on day one.

breaks.what: Three flags pulls a worker mid-month
breaks.do: Three flags pulls a wearer, not an anchor. The device comes back that hour and someone from the bench wears it the same shift. A KMSC-recruited wearer's seat goes to Mano for hiring the same day; a site-nominated wearer is replaced by the site's next nominee, through the gate. The pulled worker is never re-enrolled. The Portfolio Manager checks that the first two flags reached the worker inside 24 hours, and if not, fixes that first.
Below 10%, Moharam tells Mano the same day and hiring starts that week. No new site launches on a book with no bench.

breaks.what: A supervisor is out at a 50-phone site
breaks.do: The senior anchor named as deputy takes the sweeps. The Portfolio Manager is on that floor for the shift. Moharam sends a bench supervisor the next day.

breaks.what: Someone under 18, or without ID, reaches a floor
breaks.do: The anchor does not hand them a device; if they are wearing one, tap stop and take it off now. Tell the Portfolio Manager now. Mano runs the gate; Moharam if the site pushed the person. If any footage was recorded, the Portfolio Manager pulls the device the same hour, Youssef Medhat holds every session from it, and Mano is told the same day.
The named deputy holds the seat the same day. Gear back within 24 hours, final pay after inspection, account closed. Mano opens the seat and fixes the map the same day.

training: Anchors: two hours with their Portfolio Manager before the first shift, on a test phone, with a signed line.

Supervisors: one day with their Portfolio Manager, one full shift on the floor, with a signed line. Portfolio Managers: one week with Moharam; Mano for money and gear, Youssef Medhat for quality. Runners: one hour with Moharam. Reviewers: the calibration set with Youssef Medhat.
Quartermaster: one full day with Mano. Hub attendants: the checklist on the wall, walked once with the quartermaster.
Every deputy has done the module for the role they cover. A second strike means retraining before the device is unpaused.

questions.q: Can I bring a friend to cover my shift?
questions.a: No. Nobody works a shift without passing Mano's gate, and nobody works on your account. Refer them to Mano instead; the hire reward is yours once they are onboarded and working.

questions.q: I woke up sick at 6 AM. Am I a no-show?
questions.a: Not if you call now. Call, then message, your Portfolio Manager this minute; no reply in 20 minutes, call Moharam. The rule is 10 PM the night before: a call at 6 AM is late, and silence is a no-show. Calling gets the bench moving and Moharam hears your side.

questions.q: Why one anchor per 10 phones and not 20?
questions.a: Because one person cannot restart 20 rigs every 30 minutes and still check angles and storage. Past 10, restarts slip and flags climb, and a flag costs more than an anchor.

questions.q: Nobody told me who my deputy is.
questions.a: Ask your manager today. Every seat has one written down. If yours is blank, the map is wrong, and Mano fixes it the same day.
Until the local hire for that seat signs off on day one. It is a bridge, not a benefit, and every housed seat is counted at the weekly book review.

attendance.noShow: A no-call, no-show is immediate removal from the project. No warning steps.
